served.stem: Xenon tetrafluoride (XeF₄) is a square planar molecule with F-Xe-F angles of 90°. The central xenon has four Xe-F σ bonds and two lone pairs that occupy axial positions to minimize lone-pair/lone-pair repulsion. What hybridization is assigned to the xenon?
served.bankWhy: Steric number at Xe = 4 bonds + 2 lone pairs = 6, requiring sp³d² hybridization (octahedral electron geometry). The two lone pairs sit trans to each other (axial), leaving the four fluorines in a square plane with 90° bond angles.

answer.line: Xe carries 4 bonds and 2 lone pairs: 6 electron domains. Six domains means octahedral electron geometry, sp^{3}d^{2}.

steps: Count domains on Xe first: 4 Xe-F bonds plus 2 lone pairs make 6.
Match the count: 2 is sp, 3 is sp^{2}, 4 is sp^{3}, 5 is sp^{3}d, 6 is sp^{3}d^{2}. Hybridization follows domains, not just bonds.
Six domains sit octahedral. The two lone pairs take opposite corners, so the four F atoms lie flat: square planar.

choices.note: Six domains: one s, three p and two d orbitals.
Four bonds alone would be sp^{3}. The two lone pairs need orbitals too, which makes six domains.
sp^{3}d fits five domains, as in XeF2, SF4 or ClF3. Xe here has six.
dsp^{2} labels square planar transition-metal complexes such as Pt(NH3)2Cl2. It matches the shape, not the six domains on Xe.
sp^{3}d^{3} is seven domains, as in IF7. Xe has 4 bonds and 2 pairs, so six.

student.lockIt: Hybridization counts domains, bonded atoms plus lone pairs: 4 is sp^{3}, 5 is sp^{3}d, 6 is sp^{3}d^{2}.
